title: Least Ambiguous Set-Valued Classifiers With Bounded Error Levels
abstract: In most classification tasks, there are observations that are ambiguous and therefore difficult to correctly label. Set-valued classifiers output sets of plausible labels rather than a single label, thereby giving a more appropriate and informative treatment to the labeling of ambiguous instances. We introduce a framework for multiclass set-valued classification, where the classifiers guarantee user-defined levels of coverage or confidence (the probability that the true label is contained in the set) while minimizing the ambiguity (the expected size of the output). We first derive oracle classifiers assuming the true distribution to be known. We show that the oracle classifiers are obtained from level sets of the functions that define the conditional probability of each class. Then we develop estimators with good asymptotic and finite sample properties. The proposed estimators build on existing single-label classifiers. The optimal classifier can sometimes output the empty set, but we provide two solutions to fix this issue that are suitable for various practical needs. Supplementary materials for this article are available online.

claims.text: Set-valued classifiers can guarantee user-defined total or class-specific coverage levels while minimizing expected output size.
Optimal set-valued classifiers under bounded error constraints correspond to level sets of conditional class probability functions.
Minimizing set ambiguity under coverage constraints can result in empty prediction sets for certain feature space regions.
Split-conformal inference enables plug-in set-valued classifiers to achieve distribution-free, finite-sample coverage guarantees.
Controlling total coverage rather than class-specific coverage leads to lower coverage on minority classes when class proportions are highly imbalanced.
Accretive completion eliminates empty prediction sets by iteratively lowering class conditional probability thresholds to minimize ambiguity increments.
On the Zip Code test dataset, the split-conformal LABEL classifier achieved a test coverage of 0.98 with an average ambiguity of 1.27.
Plug-in level set estimators maintain statistical consistency as long as the number of classes grows slower than sqrt(n)/log(n).

limitations.text: The optimal set-valued classifier can output empty prediction sets when required coverage is low or classes are well separated.
Total coverage control can yield severely low coverage for low-prevalence minority classes.
Controlling pointwise conditional coverage P{Y in H(X)|X=x} >= 1-alpha for continuous variables leads to trivial classifiers that always output all classes.
Classification with reject option frameworks rely on arbitrary rejection loss parameters that lack direct practical meaning.

future_work.text: Adapt statistical consistency proofs to set-valued classifiers modified by the accretive completion procedure.
Extend the set-valued classification framework to handle large numbers of classes by organizing labels into tree structures.
Utilize regions of high ambiguity or null predictions for novel class discovery in dataset clusters.

methodologies.name: LABEL Set-Valued Classification Framework
methodologies.description: Constructs set-valued classifiers by thresholding class conditional probability estimates to minimize expected prediction set size subject to total or class-specific coverage constraints.

methodologies.name: Accretive Completion Algorithm
methodologies.description: Greedy threshold reduction algorithm that gradually expands level sets to eliminate empty prediction regions while minimizing ambiguity increase.
conditions: Presence of null region (sum of class thresholds > 1)

methodologies.name: Split-Conformal LABEL Inference
methodologies.description: Data-splitting method where base probability estimates are computed on one split and empirical quantiles are computed on the second split to ensure distribution-free finite-sample coverage.
